analysis:
Reviewed docs/provider/troubleshooting.md (base, head, and tail unit) and the one-line patch in ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift. The doc changes are a date bump, a new lifecycle-drain troubleshooting row (head line 134: drain waits 10s for a session, shutdown waits 15s per unload, `--force` interrupts only unfinished work), a new `Retrying <model> when memory frees` row (head line 168), and a `Configuration change needs a restart` row (head line 169). None of these alters a security control, an endpoint, a trust boundary or the threat model, so no threat-model update is needed. The advice stays within existing operator commands (`darkbloom restart`, `--force`). The wording says `--force` interrupts only unfinished work, which does not weaken A-016 or T-053 revocation semantics.

The Swift change adds `noteSelectedModelUnloaded(victim, by: command)` after a successful Autopilot eviction unload (ProviderLoop+Autopilot.swift head line 213). It runs after the unload-success guard, so it is only reached for a victim that was actually unloaded. From the patch alone it appears to record bookkeeping that schedules a later retry load of an explicitly selected model. The function body is not supplied, so this is unverified. Its retry path is not visible, but the doc describes limits: it unloads only idle models outside the selection, with no Autopilot hold, pin or lease, and it respects dwell and idle time. Remaining questions for integration: (1) whether the retry loader can bypass ModelLoadAdmission memory gating or the weight-hash and attestation advertisement checks. (2) Whether a retry racing with an Autopilot lease or placement hold can produce in-flight eviction (T-010, T-029). (3) Whether the retry loop's backoff, 30s to 10min, is bounded so it does not cause a DoS. The relevant threats are T-029 and T-027, with T-041 touched only indirectly (model unload and cache lifecycle). No concrete regression is demonstrable from the supplied evidence.
